 EPL: Gusto Fit for Tottenham Clash, Martinez Out for Weeks — Alonso
 By Soliu Oyesiji 2 mins read RELATED EPL: Saka to Miss Everton Clash as Arsenal Await Injury Scan Results Neto Brace Ends Everton’s Unbeaten Run as Chelsea Win 2-0 Carrick Plays Down Martinez’s Outburst, says Man United have Moved On Arsenal Beat Leeds 2-1 as Guimaraes Seals Comeback Win Arteta Hopeful on Havertz, Konsa Ahead of Leeds Clash Xabi Alonso Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has confirmed that defender Malo Gusto is available for selection ahead of the Blues’ Premier League clash against Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.
 However, Pep Chavarria, Emmanuel Emegha and goalkeeper Emi Martinez will miss the London derby as they continue their recovery from injuries.
 Chelsea head into the encounter on the back of consecutive league victories, having thrashed Bournemouth 5-1 before defeating Everton 2-0.
 Tottenham, managed by Roberto De Zerbi, secured their first Premier League victory of the campaign in their previous outing but are yet to win away from home this season.
 Speaking after Chelsea’s training session at Cobham on Friday, Alonso confirmed that Gusto was ready to return after missing the victory over Everton.
 “Malo is fine,” the Chelsea manager said.
 Providing an update on Chavarria, Alonso said the defender had increased his training workload but would not be ready for Saturday’s encounter.
 “Pep is training a little bit more, but he is not going to make it [for the Tottenham game],” he added.
 Emegha will also remain unavailable as he continues his recovery. The striker, who joined Chelsea during the summer, is yet to make an appearance for the club.
 “He’s feeling better, but we need to wait,” Alonso said.
 Advertisement Ad Feedback RELATED EPL: Saka to Miss Everton Clash as Arsenal Await Injury Scan Results Meanwhile, Martinez is expected to be sidelined for several weeks after sustaining a jaw injury during Chelsea’s victory over Everton.
 The Argentine goalkeeper was stretchered off in the second half following a collision with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite. He was subsequently taken to hospital for further assessment before undergoing surgery.
 Alonso said the goalkeeper was recovering well but would need more time before returning to action.
 “Emi is doing better,” he said.
 “He had the surgery and day by day he is feeling better, but we still need to wait. A few weeks. Hopefully, less than that, but we need to wait.”
 The Chelsea manager added that the club would continue to monitor Martinez’s recovery in consultation with medical professionals.
 “The good thing is that he is feeling better and we need to listen to his feelings, the opinions of the doctors, the specialists, the surgeons. Considering it was a bad one, he is doing well,” Alonso said.
 Chelsea will now focus on extending their winning run against their London rivals as they seek to maintain their momentum in the Premier League.
 Gusto’s availability provides a boost for Alonso, although Martinez’s absence and the injuries to other squad members could influence the manager’s selection decisions ahead of the derby.
